deed: Solomon Ashkenazi, a Jewish physician, conducted the peace negotiations between the Ottomans and Venice
title: Solomon Ashkenazi, a Jewish physician from Udine, secretly mediated the peace between the Ottomans and Venice in 1573

trailer.text: According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Solomon Ashkenazi was a physician and diplomat born in Udine, northern Italy, and according to Panciera he was a Jewish doctor-merchant-diplomat.
In 1564 he settled in Constantinople, where he served as physician and dragoman to the Venetian Bailo Marcantonio Barbaro and to the grand vizier Mehmet Sokollu.
During the war with Venice that broke out in 1570, Barbaro employed him for secret communications with the grand vizier.
After the Ottoman defeat at Lepanto, Ashkenazi conducted the preliminary negotiations that led to the peace treaty of 1573.
In 1574 the doge and the signoria in Venice formally received him, as though he were an ambassador from the sultan.

stations.title: A physician from Udine on the way to Constantinople

paragraphs.text: According to the Encyclopaedia Judaica, Solomon Ashkenazi was born in Udine, northern Italy.
He studied medicine at Padua.
Afterwards he went to Cracow.
There he served for 16 years as court physician to Sigismund Augustus.
In 1564 Ashkenazi settled in Constantinople.
He was physician and dragoman to Marcantonio Barbaro, the Venetian Bailo.
He was also physician and dragoman to the grand vizier Mehmet Sokollu.
Both sides trusted him.
He was a physician and a merchant, and thanks to his occupation he could visit both of them without attracting attention.
According to an academic article, he was called "Rabbi Salomon Ashkenazi", and was one of Sokollu's confidants in his correspondence with Barbaro.
In 1570 war broke out between the Ottomans and Venice.
According to Panciera, the War of Cyprus (1570–1573) quickly reached the Dalmatian mainland as well.
According to Panciera, the Ottomans occupied a broad swath of the districts of Zadar and Split.
In Venice itself, the situation of the Jews worsened.
On 6 March 1570 the Venetian Senate voted by a large majority to detain all Turks and Levantine Jews, and their property as well.
On 18 December 1571 the Venetian Senate decided to expel the Jews from the city after two years, but in 1573 the expulsion decree was revoked.
During that war Barbaro employed Ashkenazi for secret communications with the grand vizier.
Sokollu could not meet openly with the bailo.
The war party, including Uchalí, could accuse him of treason and remove him from power.

In Venice, despite the victory at Lepanto, ending the conflict became urgent because of its high cost, around twelve million ducats, and because of its destructive effects on the Dalmatian hinterland.
After the Ottoman defeat at Lepanto, Ashkenazi conducted the preliminary negotiations.
On 29 January 1573 he visited the bailo.
He proposed a principle that remained constant throughout the negotiations: the peace would be based on the previous Ottoman-Venetian treaty, of 1540.
Barbaro had received no new instructions from Venice, and had to accept these vague principles against his will.
Sokollu offered Barbaro perpetual peace in return for an annual tribute, harâc.
Barbaro refused without hesitation.
Two days later Sokollu demanded half a million ducats for the suspension of fighting.
He proposed the principle of uti possidetis as the basis for peace.
On 6 February 1573 Ashkenazi visited the Venetian embassy in Pera.
He reminded the bailo that three hundred galleys were waiting in the Ottoman arsenals if the condition was not accepted.
Uchalí, he said, was ready to attack the Venetian islands.
A few days later he came with news: on 8 February the Ottomans had held a war council and decided on a decisive offensive against Corfu and Zadar.

stations.title: The night the peace was written

paragraphs.text: According to the anonymous author of a relazione, on 7 March 1573 Sokollu summoned the bailo to his residence.
The bailo was also told that the dragoman and Ashkenazi would come in the night to write down the text of the agreement.
According to Noailles, the peace was concluded on Saturday, 7 March 1573.
Before that, the petition (arz) had been prepared, translated, delivered to the vizier and presented to the sultan.
According to Panciera, the peace treaty was signed in Istanbul.
According to the article, three months of lengthy negotiations culminated in the treaty of capitulations between the Ottomans and Venice.
According to Gordon, Ashkenazi demonstrated a dual loyalty to both powers, and risked his life to facilitate the signing of the treaty.
The truce cost Venice 300,000 ducats, the same as the sum given in the reign of Süleyman I.
Venice was exempted from paying 8,000 ducats a year for Cyprus, because the whole island had become Ottoman territory.
The annual tribute for the island of Zante rose from 500 to 1,500 ducats.
Venice was required to surrender to the Ottomans the castle of Sopotò, today Borsh in Albania, with its artillery.
According to Gordon, Venice signed the treaty from a position of weakness.
In the year after the peace, in 1574, Ashkenazi was sent to Venice.
He came as the vizier's personal representative, to propose an alliance to the Venetian government.
It was decided to treat him as though he were an ambassador from the sultan.
The doge and the signoria formally received him in this capacity.
He was received with great honour, and was given 1,000 sequins on his arrival.
According to Panciera, his appointment to an inspection mission in Venice and Dalmatia made him the real mediator behind the negotiations, as he had been for the peace treaty.
The mission did not settle the matter, but it helped to keep the negotiations open.

According to Panciera, during the negotiations on the peace treaty of 1573 the Sultan declared that he was opposed to handing over territories that had been captured by the sword for Islam, but the vizier nevertheless agreed to include a handover clause.

After the peace agreement was signed, in the months when the return of the territories in Dalmatia was under discussion, it was proposed to settle the dispute with an annual payment of 2,000 ducats to the Porte.
The proposal was met with a Turkish counterproposal of 20,000 sequins, an unacceptable amount.
At the end of November 1574, Ashkenazi suggested to Bailo Tiepolo that he give the Grand Vizier a gift of 10,000 ducats.
At the end of August 1575 Soranzo sought Ashkenazi's mediation.
Ashkenazi advised combining threats and bribery to convince the grand vizier.
Soranzo turned to him again, to win over the vizier, who was somewhat weary of the affair.
The Venetian diplomats put pressure on Fereydun, on Ashkenazi and on the grand vizier, so that the borders commission would start work immediately.
According to Panciera, one of the major achievements of the relations that followed was the revival of trade between Venice and the Balkans.
This trade led to the establishment of the Freeport of Split in 1590.

stations.title: Years of diplomacy, and a woman who cured a sultan

paragraphs.text: According to the Encyclopaedia, Ashkenazi claimed that he was responsible for the exertion of Turkish support when Henri de Valois was elected to the Polish throne in 1573.
In 1586 Ashkenazi signed the preliminary articles of the treaty with Spain on behalf of the sultan.
In 1591 he used his influence to have Emanuel Aron appointed voivode of Moldavia.
Aron was probably of Jewish extraction.
According to the Encyclopaedia, Ashkenazi's final diplomatic activities took place in the reign of Sultan Murad III.
Murad III's attitude to the Jews of the empire was negative.
His widow, Boula Eksati, inherited some of his medical secrets.
Early in the 17th century she cured the boy-sultan Ahmed I of smallpox.

stations.title: Doubts, prison and the end of the road

paragraphs.text: According to Panciera, around 15 September 1574 Ashkenazi carried out a hasty inspection in Zemunik, Novigrad and Poličnik, and the inspection raised doubts about his authority, because he seemed overly cautious towards the local Muslim communities.
In 1593 Ashkenazi went to Jassy, in the hope of obtaining compensation for his efforts.
There he was handed over to the prince of Transylvania and thrown into jail.
The English ambassador in Constantinople ultimately secured his release.
Ashkenazi died shortly afterwards.

versions.says: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, he was born in about 1520 and died in 1602.
According to the same source, he died shortly after his release from the jail into which he was thrown in 1593

disagreements.question: How much money was Sokollu himself to receive?

versions.says: Barbaro proposed to reward the grand vizier with 25 to 30 thousand gold pieces
According to Noailles, Sokollu was to receive 50,000 ducats in the end

claims.text: ב-1586 חתם אשכנזי בשם הסולטן על סעיפיו המקדימים של ההסכם עם ספרד.
claims.quote: In 1586 he signed the preliminary articles of the treaty with Spain on behalf of the sultan.

claims.text: ב-1591 השתמש אשכנזי בהשפעתו כדי להשיג את מינויו של עמנואל ארון, שהיה כנראה ממוצא יהודי, לוויבודה של מולדביה.
claims.quote: In 1591, he used his influence to secure the appointment as voivode of Moldavia of Emanuel Aron (who was probably of Jewish extraction).

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה, פעילותו הדיפלומטית האחרונה של אשכנזי התרחשה בימי הסולטן מוראד השלישי, שיחסו ליהודי האימפריה היה שלילי.
claims.quote: His final diplomatic activities took place under greatly changed circumstances during the reign of the Sultan Murad iii, whose attitude to the Jews in the empire was negative.

claims.text: אלמנתו של אשכנזי, בולה אקסאטי, ירשה חלק מסודותיו הרפואיים ובראשית המאה ה-17 ריפאה את הסולטן הילד אחמד הראשון מאבעבועות.
claims.quote: His widow, Boula Eksati, inherited some of his medical secrets, and early in the 17th century cured the boy-sultan Ahmed i of smallpox.

claims.text: בסביבות 15 בספטמבר 1574 ערך אשכנזי עם שני ונציאנים סיור בדיקה שטחי בזמוניק, נוביגראד ופוליצ'ניק, ועוררו ספקות לגבי סמכותו, מפני שנראה זהיר יתר על המידה כלפי הקהילות המוסלמיות המקומיות.
claims.quote: the inspection, however, raised a series of misgivings about the authoritativeness of Ashkenazi, who seemed to be excessively cautious towards the local Muslim communities.

claims.text: כשהגיע ליאשי ב-1593 בתקווה לקבל פיצוי על מאמציו, נמסר אשכנזי לנסיך טרנסילבניה והושלך לכלא.
claims.quote: When he went to Jassy in 1593 in the hope of obtaining compensation for his efforts, he was handed over to the prince of Transylvania and thrown into jail;

claims.text: שגריר אנגליה בקונסטנטינופול השיג בסופו של דבר את שחרורו של אשכנזי מהכלא, והוא מת זמן קצר לאחר מכן.
claims.quote: ultimately, the English ambassador in Constantinople secured his release. He died shortly afterwards.

claims.text: ברבארו הציע לתגמל את הווזיר הגדול על שירותיו בסכום של 25 עד 30 אלף מטבעות זהב.
claims.quote: Barbaro proposed to reward the Grand Vizier with a sum ranging from 25 to 30 thousand gold pieces for his services.

claims.text: לפי נואיי, סוקולו אמור היה לקבל בסוף 50,000 דוקטים.
claims.quote: According to Noailles, Soḳollu was to recieve 50000 ducats at the end.

claims.text: לפי פנצ'רה, בסביבות 15 בספטמבר 1574 ערך אשכנזי בדיקה חטופה בזמוניק, בנובגרד ובפוליצ'ניק, והבדיקה עוררה ספקות לגבי סמכותו, כי הוא נראה זהיר מדי כלפי הקהילות המוסלמיות המקומיות.
claims.quote: the inspection, however, raised a series of misgivings about the authoritativeness of Ashkenazi
